entry.title: On the (In)stability of Adaptive Fee Mechanisms in Multi-Chain Systems
entry.summary:
EIP-1559 has become the dominant transaction fee mechanism in permissionless blockchains, regulating scarce block space through an adaptive base fee. The design balances a trade-off between responsiveness to demand fluctuations and stability of long-term resource usage. On a single chain, this trade-off is well understood and empirically stable.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #consensus

entry.title: How Much Screening Buys a Second? Speed, Selection, and the Maker's Spread
entry.summary:
We study the spread a liquidity provider needs to break even against counterparties that can exploit a stale quote, and we place two defenses on a single scale: repricing sooner and screening informed flow. A break-even condition pins down the exact screening rate at which a slower maker matches a faster unscreened venue: the selection that buys back the extra staleness. The result requires only an integrable price innovation and therefore holds under jumps, atoms and infinite variance.

Source: Ethereum Research (ethresear.ch) · Tags: #zkp #consensus #infosec #clean-tech
